MINUTES
  PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MEETING
  JULY 19, 2021

  An adjourned meeting of the Park and Activities Commission of the City of Rolling Hills Estates
  was called to order at 6:04 p.m. in Highridge Park, 29035 Highridge Rd., Rolling Hills Estates,
  California by CHAIR POPE.

  2.  PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

  CHAIR POPE led those present in the Pledge of Allegiance.

  3.  ROLL CALL

  COMMISSIONERS PRESENT:  Bain, Ciarolla, Persichina, Pope, Retz, Romanelli

  COMMISSIONERS ABSENT:  McCormick

  STAFF PRESENT:  Alexa Davis, Assistant City Manager
  Michael Goldsmith, Maintenance Superintendent
  Daniel A-Haja, Community Services Coordinator

  4.  APPROVAL OF MINUTES

  A.  PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION REGULAR MEETING DRAFT MINUTES OF
  JUNE 21, 2021

  COMMISSIONER RETZ made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER BAIN to:

  APPROVE THE PARKS AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MINUTES OF JUNE
  21, 2021.

  There being no objection, CHAIR POPE so ordered.

  5.  AUDIENCE ITEMS NOT ON THE AGENDA

  None

  6.  BUSINESS ITEMS

  A.  HILLS ARE ALIVE UPDATE (VERBAL REPORT)

  COMMISSIONER PERSICHINA noted a new start for the 10k runners which will start
  before the 5k runners. The new emcee for the event will be CHAIR POPE. Bibs and shirts
  are currently being ordered with volunteer shirts being a separate color from the regular
  ones. Sponsorships are also on track. Assistant City Manager (ACM) Davis noted the
  lack of race director this year and low numbers of volunteers. Staff has connected with

PARK AND ACTIVITIES MEETING MINUTES  1
JULY 19, 2021
   the RHE Target to see if they may have volunteers. Maintenance Superintendent
  Goldsmith suggested to reach out to the equestrian Junior Drill Team to volunteer.
  COMMISSIONER BAIN asked why the Scouts were not available this year. ACM Davis
  replied that the two adults per two scouts ratio could not be met by the group, so they had
  to decline this year’s participation. COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI asked how many
  volunteers we are short this year. Community Services Coordinator A-Haja noted that last
  year the scouts were the only volunteers on the track so this year, staff is reaching out to
  the other volunteer pools such as high school students and volunteer groups. He also
  added that a filmed review of the track with key junctions will be available to runners before
  the race. ACM Davis added that a fitness contractor will prep the runners with a warm-up
  in the middle of the park. A juice food truck is also being researched. CHAIR POPE
  suggested reaching out to local YMCA groups to reach volunteers. COMMISSIONER
  BAIN asked if Walt Ordway was able to reach out to the equestrians for sweepers.
  COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI stated that Walt has contacted Sheryl Steckel to act as
  the sweep with an additional second sweeper. ACM Davis noted the Sheriff’s Posse will
  be available to fill gaps if needed. So far 20 runners have signed up and posters and
  signs for the event will be posted shortly.

  B.  TRACY AUSTIN DOUBLES TOURNAMENT (VERBAL REPORT)

  ACM Davis stated that staff has been waiting to hear back from Ms. Austin to confirm a
  date. Upon date confirmation from her, a subcommittee meeting will be scheduled.

  C.  CITY CELEBRATION (VERBAL REPORT)

  COMMISISONER RETZ noted the games planned this year will be conscious of COVID.
  He reported that stickers and Happy Hats for Kids are to replace face painting. The event
  date is September 25. The Poker Ride is still on and a Pepper Tree booth will be manned
  by Commission volunteers again as well. ACM Davis noted the corn pits will be replaced
  by a possible rock wall from a local vendor. CHAIR POPE noted taking away a free corn
  pit for a paid rock wall may not be desirable. ACM Davis noted a free ticket to the rock
  wall, petting zoo, or pony ride can be added to the mailers this year in addition to the free
  events such as Happy Hats for Kids. Community Services Coordinator A-Haja added that
  Home Depot will be reached out to once more, for fun build-it-yourself craft project kits.
  Maintenance Superintendent Goldsmith noted Lowe’s can also be used for craft kits as
  the City has been utilizing their services more frequently. COMMISSIONER BAIN asked
  if a food truck would be provided at the event. ACM Davis stated that Empty Saddle Club
  usually provides the food along with beverage sales for the event. The event will be
  centered to the morning as the midday temperature gets hot. COMMISSIONER BAIN
  asked about any performances by kids. ACM Davis noted the equestrian games in the
  afternoon but noted past performers like magicians or animal presenters being successful
  previously. Waste Management could come back to make edible erosion projects for kids
  as well. COMMISSIONER BAIN asked if there would be opportunities for Community
  Booths and how they would apply for a spot at the event. ACM Davis noted a list of past
  attendees such as West Vector, Cal Water, PV library District and Scouts. Community
  Services Coordinator A-Haja noted the limited space for the booths and that approximately
  nine spots would be available. ACM Davis added that the subcommittee had chosen not
  go forward with the PV Symphonic Band this year as it conflicted with the ongoing
  equestrian events and announcements. COMMISSIONER PERSICHINA asked who

PARK AND ACTIVITIES MEETING MINUTES  2
JULY 19, 2021
   would make the announcements. ACM Davis reported that a DJ was used in the past will
  be used again as they know the needs of the equestrians during the event. CHAIR POPE
  asked if the same free events to the public like the water balloon toss and watermelon
  eating contest will happen again this year. ACM Davis affirmed those activities would be
  planned. The City versus Sheriff’s volleyball game will take place at 10 a.m. instead of 1
  p.m. and volunteers are needed to play.

  D.  HIGHRIDGE PARK MURAL PROJECT

  Community Services Coordinator A-Haja provided a brief overview of the staff report.

  Marianna Desalles noted an increase in rate per square foot from $15 per square foot to
  $18 per square foot. The revised cost would be $4,550 rather than the initially proposed
  $3,500. ACM Davis noted Park Facility fees could be used and also Pepper Tree
  Foundation funds may be used with donations now that the Foundation allows for art
  projects.

  Marianna Desalles thanked the Commission and noted the Buzz Bulletin could be
  adjusted to Commission requests. COMMISSIONER BAIN asked to increase the size of
  the bulletin part of the “Buzz Bulletin” to provide for more space for community notices.
  COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI asked how the art would be placed next to the bulletin.
  CHAIR POPE suggested being able to post messages on both sides. COMMISSIONER
  PERSICHINA asked if the project will be done by local students like the Ernie Howlett
  mural. Ms. Desalles responded that the work will be done primarily by her with the help
  of a few students from the local middle school she current teaches. COMMISSIONER
  RETZ asked if a coating could be placed over the art as many people currently use tape
  on the board to post signs. Ms. Desalles responded a vinyl coating could be placed to
  prevent that and vandalism which is already in the materials cost.

  COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI asked what was needed of the Commission. ACM Davis
  stated an approval of the project along with any edits would be needed from the
  Commission to proceed with the project. The concept was approved but the budget and
  edits may be included to go forward to Council.

  COMMISSIONER BAIN asked where the corkboard would be in relation to the artwork for
  the bulletin boards and suggested the board be side by side. COMMISSIONER
  ROMANELLI suggested a top half be artwork and the bottom be corkboard. Maintenance
  Superintendent Goldsmith suggested a frame could be used around the artwork. ACM
  Davis noted the artwork would eventually get covered. CHAIR POPE preferred the
  artwork and corkboard split from top to bottom on the Childhood Memories bulletin and
  the Buzz Bulletin corkboard to be bigger. Alternate names were suggested for the Buzz
  Bulletin such as “Community Buzz” or “Bee Kind”.

  COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI asked for a final revision for a future Commission
  meeting.

  COMMISSIONER BAIN asked how long the project would take. Ms. Desalles noted that
  since no scaffolding would be needed, Ms. Desalles offered to work on the project after
  school hours.

PARK AND ACTIVITIES MEETING MINUTES  3
JULY 19, 2021
   CHAIR POPE asked if all the animals in the mural were native to the Peninsula. It was
  discussed by the Commission and Ms. Desalles to add a red fox, PV Blue butterflies and
  a coyote which were not included. CHAIR POPE asked if a “Can you Find” key could be
  added near the bottom and if there was an opportunity to apply for an educational grant
  to fund the project. COMMISSIONER BAIN also suggested that the dove could be paired
  as they are in nature. ACM Davis noted that the edits will be included, along with a mockup
  of the bulletin boards in the next Commission staff report in September so that Ms.
  Desalles does not have to draw another mural for the report.

  The Commission requested that a revised staff report return in September for
  recommendation of approval by the City Council.

  7.  COMMISSION ITEMS

  A.  ADOPT-A-PARK (VERBAL REPORT)

  ACM Davis noted a Rockbluff Park subcommittee meeting will be scheduled soon to go
  over the proposed play structure and to go back to the Commission in August.
  Maintenance Superintendent Goldsmith added that weed abatement would be going on
  in that area as well within 30 days.

  COMMISSIONER PERSICHINA asked if AYSO soccer will be playing soon. Community
  Services Coordinator A-Haja is still awaiting the schedule from AYSO contacts.

  Maintenance Superintendent Goldsmith started gopher control this week which will be
  coming in for two months a couple of times a week at all City parks and set traps and gas
  to fix the gopher problem. Signage will be posted to warn park goers of gopher flags.
  After two months, the exterminators will come back monthly.

  B.  MATTERS OF INTEREST (VERBAL REPORT)

  COMMISSIONER BAIN asked about the previous E-Bike proposal. ACM Davis explained
  that the person has not returned with his request. COMMISSIONER BAIN asked if the
  bikes could be ridden inside the parks, to which ACM Davis responded they were not
  allowed and neither are they allowed on the bridle trails.

  8.  STAFF ITEMS

  None

  9.  MATTERS OF INFORMATION

  A.  CITY COUNCIL ACTIONS OF JUNE 22, 2021

  Received and filed.

  10.  PARK TOURS

PARK AND ACTIVITIES MEETING MINUTES  4
JULY 19, 2021
   A.  HIGHRIDGE PARK

  COMMISSIONER BAIN noted the erosion on the pathway. Maintenance Superintendent
  Goldsmith responded that it is an ongoing issue and noted the decomposed granite on
  the pathway used to help fill erosion spots.

  Maintenance Superintendent Goldsmith noted the gopher traps on the fields currently
  being used. CHAIR POPE commented on the numerous gophers in previous weeks.

  CHAIR POPE asked if the exercise stations would be replaced and if they are part of the
  perimeter pathway project. ACM Davis noted they are not scheduled to be replaced in
  the immediate future.

  COMMISSIONER PERSICHINA noted cement bags near the softball field that should be
  moved. Community Services Coordinator A-Haja responded that staff will reach out to the
  PV Softball coordinator to remove them.

  11.  FUTURE AGENDA ITEMS

  A.  PICKLEBALL

  ACM Davis stated that a report will come to the Commission in the Fall pending more
  promotion of the sport at the park. The striping of pickleball courts will come to no extra
  charge when resurfacing the tennis courts. The interest for the sport has been noted, but
  not much promotion was actively done. COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI asked to have
  Tennis Pro Bob Krueger involved in the process.

  B.  CONCERTS IN THE PARK

  ACM Davis noted staff has researched nearby cities such as Rancho Palos Verdes who
  hold similar events. The month of August would not be viable to hold such an event due
  to the process of approvals needed. October day-time concert with a Halloween theme
  will be recommended. A report will be brought to the Commission in August. October is
  also the time of the Prepared Peninsula Expo and also may be the time of the Tracy Austin
  Doubles Tennis Tournament.

  COMMISSIONER PERSICHINA asked if this year’s Holiday Parade would be the same
  as last year at Ernie Howlett Park. ACM Davis responded that the parade subcommittee
  will meet soon to discuss the event. A contract with Pageantry has already been acquired
  for review and a parade grand marshal was contacted. The event itself is supposed to
  highlight the commercial district, so the traditional parade is generally preferred over the
  drive-thru event at Ernie Howlett Park.  A snow day event as proposed by
  COMMISSIONER MCCORMICK is also being researched by staff.

PARK AND ACTIVITIES MEETING MINUTES  5
JULY 19, 2021
   12.  ADJOURNMENT

  The Park and Activities Commission concluded the meeting as a result of a disruption at
  Highridge Park requiring law enforcement and paramedic attention.

  CHAIR POPE made a motion to,

  ADJOURN THE MEETING AT 6:53 PM TO THE NEXT ADJOURNED PARK AND
  ACTIVITIES MEETING ON AUGUST 16, 2021 AT 6:00 P.M., WHICH WILL MEET
  AT LINDEN H. CHANDLER PRESERVE.

  There being no objection, CHAIR POPE so ordered.

  Respectfully submitted,  Approved,

  __________________________  _____________________________
  Daniel A-Haja  Lisa Pope
  Community Services Coordinator  Park & Activities Commission Chair

PARK AND ACTIVITIES MEETING MINUTES  6
JULY 19, 2021
